rationale: A wins because it keeps the story on a leash. Its angle, "Canva says it has 220M monthly users and 24,000 paying teams - what does that actually convert to in enterprise?" is a real skeptical reporter frame with the missing proof named out loud. B has useful instincts, but it keeps writing checks the facts cannot cash with lines like "220 million users already inside companies" and "so the legal team can make a slide deck without asking design." That is not color; that is invented furniture.
gaps_in_A: "now it's the engine inside an enterprise pitch" overstates the AI acquisition link. The update says Canva recently acquired an AI image-generation startup; it does not say that startup powers this tool.

"The acquisition and the AI-powered Enterprise launch are being connected in the same announcement" is too confident. The facts say both things are true, not that Canva connected them in the announcement.

It misses a clean private-company finance angle around "privately held, profitable, and last valued at $26B." A touches those facts in the metrics angle but does not turn them into a distinct investor/finance story.

The next step, "newsjack-detector," is less useful than proof-gathering and journalist-fit-check once the launch itself is the peg. Do not go hunting for a news peg while the launch is sitting on the desk.
gaps_in_B: "220 million users already inside companies" is invented. The update says 220 million monthly users, not workplace users, enterprise users, or company-seat penetration.
"so the legal team can make a slide deck without asking design" is made-up scene work. No legal team, slide-deck workflow, or non-designer enterprise persona appears in the facts.

"Notion, Figma, and Miro ran the same arc. Canva is the largest consumer-originated design tool to attempt it." This may be plausible analyst color, but it is unsupported here and the superlative is begging to be fact-checked into a ditch.

"Enterprise contracts introduce stickier, higher-ASP revenue and reduce churn risk" treats a product launch as proven contract economics. The announcement discloses no enterprise contract terms, pricing, churn, ASP, or named customers.
